_note: VERIFY BEFORE PRODUCTION. Org names/cities/service types are real; fill phones/addresses/hours via growth agent + admin review.

resources.name: Share Our Selves
resources.description: Community health center and social services: low-cost/free medical, dental, mental health, emergency food, and CalFresh/Medi-Cal enrollment help.

resources.name: Serve the People
resources.description: Medical, dental, vision clinic, food pantry, and benefits enrollment in a garden setting.

resources.name: Hurtt Family Health Clinic
resources.description: Federally qualified health center: medical, dental, behavioral health. Sliding scale for uninsured.

resources.name: Camino Health Center
resources.description: Federally qualified health center: medical, dental, behavioral health.
resources.city: San Clemente (also San Juan Capistrano, Lake Forest)

resources.name: Lestonnac Free Clinic
resources.description: Free medical care for uninsured and low-income residents, largely volunteer-run.
resources.hours: Limited clinic days — call or check the site

resources.name: AltaMed Health Services
resources.description: Large community clinic network: medical, dental, behavioral health, benefits enrollment.

resources.name: Families Together of Orange County
resources.description: Community clinic with homeless care navigation: medical, behavioral health, urgent care.

resources.name: KCS Health Center
resources.description: Community clinic with bilingual (Korean/English) staff: medical, dental, behavioral health.

resources.name: The Cambodian Family
resources.description: Bilingual health and mental health services rooted in OC's Cambodian community; open to all.

resources.name: NAMI Orange County
resources.description: Peer support groups, classes, and helpline for people with mental illness and their families.

resources.name: Mental Health Association of Orange County
resources.description: Direct services including homeless outreach, day services, and case management for adults with mental illness.
resources.eligibility: Adults with serious mental illness; varies by program

resources.name: OC2EMG Advocacy — waymakers
resources.description: Free advocacy and services for victims of any crime or abuse, including help with restraining orders and court support.

resources.name: Legal Aid Society of Orange County
resources.description: Free civil legal help for low-income residents: eviction defense, benefits appeals, family law, consumer issues.

resources.name: Public Law Center
resources.description: Free civil legal services: housing, immigration, veterans' benefits, homeless rights (including the Orange County homeless litigation advocacy).

resources.name: OC Public Defender
resources.description: Free criminal defense for those who can't afford an attorney. If you have open warrants or charges, they can help clear them.

resources.name: Working Wardrobes
resources.description: Free career services, resume help, and professional clothing for people re-entering the workforce.

resources.name: OC One-Stop Centers
resources.description: Free job search help, training programs, resume support, and benefits assistance. Multiple locations countywide.

resources.name: Volunteers of America Los Angeles — Veterans Services
resources.description: SSVF program: rapid rehousing and homeless prevention for veterans and veteran families.

resources.name: Goodwill of Orange County
resources.description: Job training and employment services, including for people with barriers like homelessness and justice involvement.

resources.name: Chrysalis OC
resources.description: Employment services built for people with low income, homelessness, or justice involvement — job-readiness classes, paid transitional jobs.

resources.name: Vital Brain Health / H.O.M.E.S. Inc
resources.description: Affordable and supported housing for adults recovering from mental illness, plus life skills support.
resources.eligibility: Adults with mental illness; varies by program

resources.name: Telecare Orange County (Crisis Residential / Court eval services)
resources.description: Short-term crisis residential treatment as an alternative to hospitalization. County-contracted program.
resources.eligibility: Adults in mental health crisis; often via OC Links or county referral

resources.name: OC Regional / OC Animal Care (for people with pets)
resources.description: People fleeing homelessness or DV should know shelters like Grandma's House of Hope and some DV shelters accept pets; OC Animal Care can also help in a pinch.

resources.name: 211 OC Help Chatbot & Text Line
resources.description: Text your ZIP to 898211 for 211 OC services by text. Useful when phone calls are hard.
